text:
My read: **Trellis (ADR-0075) is a reconciliation substrate for the reactive *read* side** — graph transactions, dependency identity, collection diffs, scoped teardown, output-frame lifecycle, deterministic replay — living *below typed read sessions*. The wallet operation journal is a different animal: a **durable write-side saga** (`Draft→MintPending→MintSettled→PublishPending→Settled/Unknown/Failed`) whose whole job is crash-recovery and reconciling against *external* authority (the mint) so no double-spend/double-pay survives process death. [...] ## No — don't build the wallet money-safety journal on Trellis. (The read projection already rides it.)

**The one fact that settles it:** Trellis graphs are **in-memory, per-session, and die with the process by design** — built fresh in `FeedSessionTrellisAdapter::new`, torn down on `close_scope`, with zero persistence in `trellis-core`. The wallet journal's *entire reason to exist* is surviving process death after an irreversible external effect (a mint spend). Trellis can't even represent that problem, let alone solve it. [...] | | Trellis (ADR-0075) | Wallet operation journal |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | Reactive **read** dependency-graph reconciliation | Durable **write** saga with external side effects |
| Semantics | **Convergent + declarative** — diff desired vs. actual; *close is always safe, reopen always possible* | **Monotonic + effectful** — states only advance; *a mint spend can't be "closed"*; at-most-once |
| "Reconcile on restart" | Replay a trace, check incremental recompute == full recompute (deterministic, local) | Query the **mint** (external authority) for proof state, then publish or unlock (non-deterministic, remote) |
| Persistence / I/O | Owns none — ADR-0075 assigns I/O, store, actor integration to **NMP** | *Is* the whole point |
